note: Wed 26 Aug 2026, ~07:02 SGT pre-Asia-open run (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30 SGT). Latest completed US session is Tuesday 25 Aug (S&P +0.32% to 7677.28, VIX down to 15.45, from the already-fetched price spine). Today is a heavy event-risk day: AUD CPI 09:30 SGT, then US Core PCE + Prelim GDP at 20:30 SGT and Nvidia FQ2 earnings after the US close -- all still pending as this file is written. Monday's Iran-sanctions story escalated Tuesday with specific China/HK entities actually named, replacing the prior file's 'warned but not targeted' framing. Nine of eleven items below are dated 25-26 Aug.

items.headline: Iran sanctions escalate: Treasury actually names China/HK entities (Sweet Ocean Industrial network), Beijing threatens retaliation
items.summary: Tuesday's follow-through on Monday's 'Operation Economic Outcast' rollout named specific mainland China and Hong Kong firms -- a Hong Kong-based procurement network including Sweet Ocean Industrial Ltd, Shenzhen Sweet Ocean Technology, RPT Technology, Tiany Technology and MT Trading and Logistics HK, plus three Chinese nationals -- accused of funneling laser-optics equipment to an Iranian defense-linked university, though major Chinese banks were again spared. Beijing's Foreign Ministry (Lin Jian) gave its first official response, saying its Iran relationship 'should not be disrupted or undermined' and vowing 'all necessary measures' to protect its interests, while Bloomberg reports Xi is signaling defiance rather than compliance.
items.actionable: This is the concrete escalation the book was watching for -- named HK entities (even if not systemic banks) plus a Beijing retaliation threat raises genuine tail risk for the HK tech sleeve (0700.HK/0981.HK/1810.HK); it also reinforces the geopolitical bid under gold/silver as a hedge.

items.headline: Gold prints a fresh 3-month high (~$4,697-4,710/oz), silver holds near $69.26 as Treasury-buyback dollar weakness keeps extending
items.summary: December gold futures opened Tuesday at $4,710.10 (+0.3%), with spot trading around $4,697.60 by mid-morning -- up 6.7% on the week, 15.8% on the month and 39.9% year-on-year. Drivers cited: continued Middle East geopolitical risk, the Treasury's expanded long-term bond buyback program weighing on the dollar, and persistent global inflation concerns ahead of today's PCE/GDP prints and Friday's Warsh Jackson Hole debut. Silver's ask price was $69.26, up $0.37 on the session.
items.actionable: The breakout extended for a second straight session into today's PCE/GDP and Nvidia prints -- no reason to de-risk the miners sleeve pre-Asia-open; Friday's Warsh tone remains the bigger swing factor than today's macro data.

items.headline: US Consumer Confidence misses badly: 89.4 vs 90.3 expected, weakest since January; Expectations Index falls into recession-signal territory
items.summary: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index fell 0.8 points to 89.4 in August (vs 90.3 consensus, 90.2 revised prior), the weakest reading since January. The Expectations sub-index dropped 5.8 points to 68.2 -- below the 80 threshold the Conference Board says has historically preceded a recession within a year -- even as the Present Situation index rose 6.8 points to 121.2 on a three-month streak-breaking bounce.
items.actionable: A soft-landing-doubt data point landing right before today's PCE/GDP and Friday's Warsh speech -- reinforces the case for staying long the metals hedge and patient on the cash pile rather than chasing risk into a data-heavy 48 hours.

items.headline: Nvidia's FQ2 print lands today after the US close -- consensus $2.09 EPS on ~$92-95bn revenue (+97% y/y), the week's cleanest AI-capex read
items.summary: Nvidia reports fiscal Q2 2027 results after the close Wednesday 26 Aug (~4:20-4:30pm ET), with Wall Street modeling EPS of roughly $2.09 (nearly double a year ago) and revenue in the $92-95bn range on continued Data Center/Blackwell demand; 58 of 61 covering analysts rate it Buy or Strong Buy. Still pending as of this writing.
items.actionable: No direct book exposure to Nvidia, but the print sets the risk-on/off tone for HK tech and broader Asia sentiment at tomorrow's open -- a binary, dated catalyst worth watching passively rather than trading around blind.

items.headline: Oil extends its slide (WTI ~$81, Brent below $89) as Iran and Oman float an 'interim framework' to reopen Hormuz shipping
items.summary: WTI traded near $81/bbl (down roughly 6% over three sessions) and Brent closed below $89 Tuesday as Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi and Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi discussed a 'temporary joint maritime corridor' to resume Strait of Hormuz shipping, per a joint statement carried by Oman News Agency -- a genuine diplomatic step beyond Secretary Rubio's earlier 'progress but not finality' comments.
items.actionable: A real de-escalation signal (not just profit-taking) -- if the corridor talks hold, it removes one geopolitical leg from the gold/silver bid even as the Treasury-buyback dollar-debasement driver stays intact, so don't extrapolate this into a broader risk-off reversal for the metals sleeve.

items.headline: Bitcoin breaks $80,000 for the first time since mid-May on the same debasement/short-covering narrative lifting gold
items.summary: BTC opened Tuesday at $78,982 (+1.6% on Monday's open), climbed as high as $81,023 intraday before pulling back, and traded around $79,000-80,000 through the session -- its highest level since May, per Bloomberg, on continued short-covering and the same dollar-weakness narrative driving gold and silver rather than an independent crypto catalyst.
items.actionable: BTC confirmed the break of $80k the book flagged as the next technical level -- still best read as a levered extension of the metals trade rather than a diversifier, so it doesn't change the case for the gold/silver miners sleeve either way.

items.headline: STI rallies ~1% to 5,735.68 Tuesday, tracking regional gains on US-Iran talks; DBS/UOB/Singtel all higher
items.summary: The Straits Times Index closed at 5,735.68, up 55.22 points (~1%), with local press attributing the move to broader regional gains as investors tracked the US-Iran diplomatic developments. DBS closed at S$76.40 (+1.11%), UOB at S$41.11 (+0.93%) and Singtel at S$4.49 (+1.58%); smaller-cap movers included Kingsmen Creatives (+~2% on a S$30m NS-gallery contract) and Samudera Shipping.
items.actionable: The SGX banks/telecom sleeve (D05/O39/Z74) is riding the same regional risk-on tape as HK tech and the metals trade -- a broad-based session rather than a Singapore-specific catalyst, so no rebalancing signal here.

items.headline: Lynas Rare Earths' FY26 full-year results due today; comes as China tightens rare-earth export licensing enforcement
items.summary: Lynas releases full-year results for the period to 30 June 2026 today (26 Aug), with interim CEO Pol Le Roux hosting an analyst webcast -- the first scorecard since its Malaysian heavy-rare-earth plant began samarium production in April. Separately, recent Chinese enforcement actions (a June detention of a precision-optics executive over mislabeled germanium exports, new MOFCOM licensing catalogue additions covering samarium, gadolinium and lutetium compounds) signal Beijing is actively tightening rare-earth export controls even as it opposes the new Iran sanctions.
items.actionable: Tighter Chinese licensing enforcement is structurally bullish for the non-China rare-earth watchlist (LYC.AX/MP/UUUU) longer-term, but today's Lynas print is the near-term swing factor for LYC.AX specifically -- watch for margin/production commentary rather than trading the export-control headline alone.

items.headline: Xiaomi's self-developed chip push continues to divide analysts: 3nm flagship processor unveiled, but stock down 17% over 90 days on margin concerns
items.summary: Xiaomi's newly announced in-house smartphone, AI and self-driving chips remain its most aggressive semiconductor self-sufficiency push, but the stock has fallen 17% over the past 90 days to roughly HK$25.62, with at least one analyst cutting its fair-value estimate from ~HK$44.93 to ~HK$38.12 on weaker Q1 EBIT and smartphone-segment margin/revenue concerns.
items.actionable: The chip story is a genuine long-term catalyst but hasn't stopped the stock's slide -- still watching for confirmation SMIC is the fab partner, which would be the cleaner 0981.HK trade than chasing 1810.HK on the chip headline alone.

items.headline: Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole keynote (his first as Fed Chair) themed 'Financial Innovation' -- no forward guidance expected, biggest single event risk of the week
items.summary: The Jackson Hole symposium's 2026 theme, 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' points toward CBDC/stablecoin/payments content rather than explicit rate signaling; Warsh has already stripped forward guidance from FOMC statements and told reporters his remarks will focus on 'long-term structural questions.' Inflation still running around 3.4% y/y keeps the hawk/dove debate live into Friday.
items.actionable: Bigger event risk for the metals trade than today's PCE/GDP or Nvidia -- Friday's tone (not today's data) is the swing factor for whether the gold/silver breakout extends or reverses; avoid adding fresh leverage into it.

items.headline: AUD CPI due 09:30 SGT today (before Asia's open): consensus 3.2-3.3% y/y, trimmed mean ~3.5% -- sets the tone for the RBA's September decision
items.summary: Australia's July monthly CPI indicator is due at 11:30am AEST (09:30 SGT) today, with CBA/ANZ forecasting 3.2% headline and NAB/Westpac 3.3% (down from June's 3.8% on fuel base effects), while all four majors expect the RBA's preferred trimmed-mean measure to ease only slightly to ~3.5% from 3.6%. Currency markets are positioned to react more to the trimmed-mean outcome than the flagged headline decline.
items.actionable: A hot trimmed-mean print would reopen RBA-tightening debate and pressure AUD-denominated miners (LYC.AX/ILU.AX) right at the pre-open; still pending as this file was written, so treat as a flag rather than a signal until the number lands.
